transcript.text: Alright, let's get the stability sprint planning started. We've got a ten-business-day sprint with capacity for one primary technical-debt focus, and three candidates on the table: legacy_csv_exporter, webhook_retry_service, and admin_search_index. Before I lock the plan, I want to do our normal round-robin check-in. Backend engineering, security engineering, and customer support — let's hear your input on which of these three should be the priority. Who wants to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While finishing an unrelated export ticket this afternoon, I confirmed that legacy_csv_exporter already has six of its eight endpoint migrations completed. Exactly two endpoints remain, and the backend team can finish those two within this sprint. I haven't updated the planning board yet, but this means legacy_csv_exporter is much closer to completion than the board likely reflects.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something urgent on legacy_csv_exporter. Minutes ago I confirmed in the dependency scanner that legacy_csv_exporter still packages libxml 3.9.4, which has a known exploitable parsing vulnerability. The approved remediation target is exactly libxml 4.1.0. I was verifying scanner results and haven't filed the security finding yet, but this is an active vulnerability in a component we're considering for the sprint focus.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have something important to add on legacy_csv_exporter from the customer support side. During a customer call this morning, I confirmed that exactly 42 enterprise accounts still depend on legacy_csv_exporter's old audit-column behavior. Those accounts need a migration guide before the new behavior is enabled. I recorded the call in a support note that hasn't synced to the sprint-planning system yet, so this wouldn't be visible to anyone looking at the board.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Complete the remaining two endpoint migrations for legacy_csv_exporter within the ten-business-day sprint.
Upgrade the bundled libxml dependency from 3.9.4 to the approved remediation target 4.1.0 as part of the sprint focus, and file the security finding in the tracker.
Produce and distribute a migration guide covering the old audit-column behavior change for the 42 enterprise accounts before enabling the new behavior.
Update the planning board to reflect the six completed endpoint migrations, the active security finding, and the customer-support dependency note.
